tasks.title: Add exact AI Assistant summary transport
tasks.description: REQ-010, REQ-030, REQ-031, REQ-032, REQ-033, REQ-034, REQ-035, FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-6, DR-1, DR-3, REQ-042, REQ-043, REQ-056, PR-1, PR-2, PR-3, AC-1, AC-4, and AC-10 / Component: AI Assistant transport and outbound serialization - use the exact exported class symbol ApiAIAssistant from the exact case-sensitive module path packages/@webex/contact-center/src/services/ApiAiAssistant.ts (the filename casing does not rename the live symbol); add ApiAIAssistant.sendSummaryGetEvent and sendSummaryResponseEvent, with package-internal SummaryGetEventName and SummaryResponseEventName aliases in ApiAiAssistant.ts derived from the six AIAssistantEventName member value types rather than repeated string literals, reusing getBaseUrl, credentials, /event, POST, auth, getErrorDetails, core TIMEOUT_REQ, and package-internal AI_ASSISTANT_CLIENT_TYPE. In ApiAiAssistant.ts, declare package-internal source-module exports AI_SUMMARY_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS = TIMEOUT_REQ and AI_SUMMARY_TRANSPORT_ERROR_CODES with exact VALIDATION_FAILED = AI_SUMMARY_TRANSPORT_VALIDATION_FAILED, HTTP_REQUEST_FAILED = AI_SUMMARY_HTTP_REQUEST_FAILED, and TIMEOUT = AI_SUMMARY_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT values; omit both from the package root. Add one private buildSummaryEventEnvelope helper with a discriminated GET/response input; both public methods must call it, it alone constructs every HTTP body level field-by-field with no caller-object or partial-object spread, it writes the shared agentId/orgId/eventType/eventName/publishTimestamp/eventDetails.data identifier/clientType/actionTimeStamp envelope, and its response branch selects only the allowed flow fields. Reject a missing/unknown base URL with root-exported AI_SUMMARY_ERROR_CODES.AI_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL_NOT_AVAILABLE in both Error.message and data.errorCode. Inside both async methods, reject rather than synchronously throw with exact transport VALIDATION_FAILED message/data.errorCode for empty agentId, derived orgId, interactionId, or conversationId, an event name outside that method's three-member union, or invalid response timestamps; perform this validation before base-URL resolution, body construction, timers, and webex.request. Serialize independently derived conversationId and interactionId without collapsing them. For GET requests, capture one Date.now() value for both timestamps. For responses, preserve independently supplied finite non-negative actionTimeStamp and publishTimestamp values, capture one fallback Date.now() per call, and use it only for omitted fields. Omit the SDK-only summaryReceived discriminator; a mid-call body must have no wrapUpCode key and a post-call body no agentName key, including no undefined-valued key. Add one private bounded-post helper used by both methods: make one webex.request attempt with timeout: AI_SUMMARY_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS, race it with one same-duration guard so an injected never-settling Promise still settles, attach the late rejection handler immediately, clear the guard in finally, return void on success, normalize the guard or exact ETIMEDOUT result to transport TIMEOUT, and never retry. For every other HTTP rejection, read only an optional finite numeric top-level statusCode, discard the original error, create a fresh projection from the bounded request-failure code, method/event, and safe identifiers, and pass only that projection to getErrorDetails or diagnostics; never forward or stringify the original message, stack, request, options, body, response, details, or cause. Extend the existing case-sensitive ApiAiAssistant Jest target with complete toStrictEqual request-object tests for all six names through the shared builder, not.toHaveProperty assertions for every flow-invalid key, request clock reuse, distinct supplied response timestamps, one-field/two-field fallback, post-call/consult/transfer/cancel happy paths, Promise-only table-driven validation rejection with no HTTP for every empty identifier and both out-of-union event directions, one HTTP attempt carrying the timeout, fake-timer TIMEOUT rejection and zero stale guards for never-resolving GET and response paths, and a privacy case whose rejected error carries the serialized body through message/request/options/response/cause while the returned error and every logger/metric spy remain sentinel-free. The focused adapter suite is acceptance evidence only for the outbound-serialization portion of AC-1, the cancellation-serialization portion of AC-4, and the adapter privacy boundary of AC-10; AC-2/AC-3 Promise settlement and response-before-handoff assertions remain with Task, realtime coordination, and consumer-sequencing verification. This task is the REQ-056 sanitized HTTP-failure and bounded-transport implementation owner and depends on define-ai-summary-contracts for exact discriminants, transport types, public/internal export boundaries, and the client-type constant.

tasks.title: Coordinate pending requests and receiving-agent delivery
tasks.description: G-3, G-4, REQ-006, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-012, REQ-028, REQ-029, REQ-037, REQ-038, REQ-039, FR-1, FR-2, FR-4, FR-8, FR-9, FR-10, FR-11, FR-12, DR-5, REQ-044, REQ-045, REQ-046, REQ-047, REQ-048, REQ-056, PR-1, PR-2, PR-3, AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-5, AC-6, AC-7, AC-8, AC-9, AC-10, and AC-11 / Component: Realtime coordination, correlation, and receiver delivery - add getAISummaryCorrelation with the exact {conversationId, interactionId} return shape (conversationId = mainInteractionId ?? interactionId; interactionId = the task's top-level interactionId) and a package-internal AISummaryCoordinator implementing the narrow request-coordinator interface. TaskManager lifecycle-owns one coordinator and the FR-11 request, FR-8 receiver-buffer, and orphan-feature timer/lifecycle policies, while AISummaryCoordinator directly owns the event-type-indexed pendingAISummaryRequests registry, receivingSummaryBuffer, interactionFeatureEnablement, and all timer handles. Arm the request timer only with accepted pending insertion, the receiver timer only with buffer insertion/replacement, and the feature timer only for a snapshot whose canonical interaction key has no registered task; clear required or optional timers through removeTimedEntry before settlement, cancellation, timeout, replacement, promotion, delivery, expiry, task cleanup, or SDK cleanup. Preserve the semantic aliases backed by the single AI_SUMMARY_DURATION_MS value, exact validated event-type correlation, timeout/overlap/late-event outcomes, latest-only buffering, ambiguity protection, and scoped/full cleanup. For a valid subsequent-agent payload with zero or multiple matching registered tasks, routeReceivingSummary replaces the per-conversation buffer with the latest payload and arms/rearms its 30-second timer. After TaskManager inserts or updates a task, it calls retainFeatureEnablementForTask with the canonical interaction key before emitting its incoming/hydrate lifecycle event; after that event it recomputes the conversation candidate set and calls flushReceivingSummary, where exactly one candidate makes the coordinator clear the buffer/timer before one delivery and zero or multiple candidates retain it. Delivery, expiry, scoped task cleanup, and full SDK cleanup all remove receiver state through the same private removeTimedEntry helper; task removal and SDK deregistration both reach that path. Use payload.interactionId as the feature map key only when it represents the same top-level interaction ID returned by getAISummaryCorrelation(task.data).interactionId; writer presence checks, Task gating, task-registration promotion, and final-task cleanup all use that exact derivation and never the conversation key. Store an unmatched feature snapshot with the shared 30-second orphan timer, remove that timer when a matching task registers, retain active state only for the matching task lifecycle, and clear every form during full cleanup. TaskManager remains the raw double-envelope parser and task-registry owner, holds the current profile-derived ConfigFlags view, exposes the bound getGeneratedSummaryFlags accessor injected into every Task, composes exactly one coordinator for its own lifetime, derives complete conversation-matching task candidate sets, and delegates only validated payloads/state transitions while preserving transcript and suggested-response routing. Represent the logical pending key of conversationId plus inbound summary type as a conversation-keyed map per event type because FR-9 exposes no task/request identifier; make each entry generic in its event type so its resolver accepts exactly AISummaryPayloadByInboundType[T] and the paired async registration returns AISummaryPendingRegistration<T>, whose result is that exact Promise payload without a Task assertion. Implement registerPendingAISummaryRequest as an async method with no internal await: atomically check the key, reject its registration Promise with augmented AI_SUMMARY_REQUEST_ALREADY_PENDING before constructing an inbound-result Promise, insertion, or timer arm when occupied, otherwise insert and resolve with the result-Promise handle; Task awaits acceptance before HTTP, so overlap cannot start HTTP. Require taskId on registration and cancellation as the ownership guard, so cancellation and per-task cleanup are no-ops for a sibling owner's entry. Treat CONSULT and TRANSFER as one MID_CALL_SUMMARY slot despite their distinct outbound names. Count every parsed frame classified as FEATURE_ENABLEMENT once before payload validation, including repeated and payload-invalid frames; forward/store only valid payloads and exclude unparseable or unclassifiable frames from that metric. For every valid FEATURE_ENABLEMENT payload, TaskManager's raw RTD parser calls AISummaryCoordinator.setFeatureEnablement(payload, hasRegisteredTask) before emitting AGENT_EVENTS.FEATURE_ENABLEMENT through TaskManager's EventEmitter without importing ContactCenter; Task request gating reads the latest snapshot through the injected coordinator's getFeatureEnablement accessor using the same canonical top-level interaction key. Implement the complete coordinator surface from the design inventory: getFeatureEnablement, async registerPendingAISummaryRequest, cancelPendingAISummaryRequest, setFeatureEnablement, retainFeatureEnablementForTask, clearFeatureEnablement, resolvePendingAISummaryRequest, routeReceivingSummary, flushReceivingSummary, clearTaskAISummaryState, and clearAISummaryState. Emit AI_SUMMARY_INBOUND_EVENT_DROPPED exactly once with a bounded reason for each malformed, unknown, late, or uncorrelated summary frame, without double-counting classified invalid feature frames. For malformed, late, uncorrelated, and buffered receiver input, log or metric only bounded event/outcome metadata and never summary text, section values, Adaptive Card bodies, raw envelopes, or arbitrary exception text. Add direct AISummaryCoordinator fake-timer and typed-contract tests for exact post-call/mid-call payload inference without assertions, the exact request/buffer/orphan-feature arm points, resolver, Promise-only overlap rejection from awaited registration with no new result Promise or timer, first-entry retention, owner cleanup, canonical feature-key writer/reader/registration/cleanup parity, orphan replacement/expiry and task promotion, buffer-on-miss, replacement, registration-triggered flush/delivery, expiry, scoped/full cleanup, ambiguity, privacy, shared-duration boundaries, exact exported timeout/overlap codes, and no stale timers on every cleanup path; keep TaskManager tests focused on parsing, validation, delegation, candidate selection, flush after task registration/listener availability, proof that legacy initiator aliases are never emitted, metrics, lifecycle integration, and regressions; retain TaskUtils correlation tests. This task owns the realtime slices of REQ-010, REQ-056, and PR-3: timeout, unknown-task, malformed/uncorrelated/late-event isolation, scoped/full cleanup, and the named AC state/RTD assertions; it does not claim public Task selection, adapter serialization, or consumer sequencing. It depends only on contract types so it can proceed independently of HTTP transport.

tasks.description: G-1, G-2, G-4, G-5, REQ-005, REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-021, REQ-022, REQ-023, REQ-024, REQ-025, FR-1, FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-6, FR-7, FR-10, FR-11, FR-12, DR-1, DR-2, DR-3, DR-4, REQ-040, REQ-041, REQ-042, REQ-043, REQ-044, REQ-045, REQ-049, REQ-050, REQ-056, PR-1, PR-2, AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-6, AC-7, AC-8, AC-10, and AC-11 / Component: Public contracts and task API plus Change: Consumer sequencing and response semantics - implement Task.configureAISummary, requestPostCallSummary, sendPostCallSummaryResponse, requestMidCallSummary, and sendMidCallSummaryResponse as additive inherited Task methods; validate structured-or-text/empty shapes using the required mid-call summaryReceived: true | false discriminant, finite non-negative counters, optional finite non-negative actionTimeStamp/publishTimestamp fields, closed action/state/feedback vocabularies, non-empty post-call wrapUpCode, and non-empty mid-call agentName; derive distinct conversationId and top-level interactionId through getAISummaryCorrelation. Call the injected getGeneratedSummaryFlags accessor on every request so Tasks created before setConfigFlags refreshes still observe the current organization kill switches. For post-call, derive interactionId as the canonical top-level value from getAISummaryCorrelation and require both current wrapUpSummariesEnabled and the latest per-interaction postCallEnabled read through coordinator.getFeatureEnablement(interactionId) to be exactly true or reject POST_CALL_SUMMARY_DISABLED; for mid-call, require current consultTransferSummariesEnabled and the latest per-interaction midCallEnabled read through the same coordinator getter to be exactly true or reject MID_CALL_SUMMARY_DISABLED; each disabled path creates no pending entry/timer and makes no HTTP call. Before HTTP, initialize a call-local registrationAccepted flag to false and await registerPendingAISummaryRequest with the literal inbound type and paired timeout code so TypeScript infers AISummaryPendingRegistration<T> and its exact Promise<PostCallSummaryEventPayload> or Promise<MidCallSummaryEventPayload> result without a type argument or assertion; set the flag true only after the handle is accepted. AI_SUMMARY_REQUEST_ALREADY_PENDING rejects that awaited registration, so it cannot reach HTTP. Catch-path cancellation calls cancelPendingAISummaryRequest(taskId, conversationId, inboundType) only when this call registered successfully; HTTP rejection therefore clears this call's owner-matched resolver/timer before rethrowing the same adapter error, while overlap performs no cancellation even for the same Task owner and leaves the first request pending. Select exact variants; pass counters and either supplied response timestamp independently and unchanged through a newly constructed whitelist object; never spread the caller payload; and emit exactly one final metric per public operation without summary text, section values, Adaptive Card bodies, agentName, raw payloads, or arbitrary exception text. Make package-internal Task.configureAISummary the sole injection point: immediately after every TaskFactory.createTask call and before listener setup or registry insertion, TaskManager passes its one lifetime-scoped AISummaryCoordinator through the AISummaryRequestCoordinator contract plus its bound GeneratedSummaryFlagsAccessor. Extend Task tests with mid-call discriminator branch, invalid/missing discriminator, transport-omission assertions, received MID_CALL_CANCELLED viewed-zero acceptance, optional timestamp pass-through on every response branch, and string/NaN/infinite/negative timestamp rejection before transport; per-invocation/live-update organization-accessor assertions; exact post-call and mid-call two-flag disabled codes with no registration/timer/HTTP; payload-boundary sentinels; exact post-call and mid-call fake-timer timeout rejection through the public Promise followed by a matching late event that cannot resettle or add another metric; one-metric-per-outcome assertions including exactly one timeout failure metric; privacy sentinels absent from every Task logger and metric spy argument across success and failure paths; exact root-exported disabled/base-URL/timeout/overlap Error.message and data.errorCode propagation, HTTP-rejection owner cancellation with no stale pending entry/timer plus an immediate same-key sequential request, pending CONSULT followed by TRANSFER Promise-only overlap rejection from awaited registration with no second HTTP call or cancellation and the first result Promise/timer still pending, additive public-surface checks including public timestamp fields and absence of internal coordinator-mapping/transport/client-type named root exports, cancellation behavior, and existing task API regressions; retain focused TaskManager composition coverage. This task owns REQ-056 disabled, base-URL, HTTP-cleanup, and overlap rejection behavior and the named public-API AC assertions. It depends on both the adapter and coordinator because Task composes those contracts.
